title: Olivia Rodrigo's Unraveled Tour: How to Snag Tickets Before They Vanish
summary: Olivia Rodrigo is hitting the road again, and this time it's the Unraveled Tour. Starting September 25 at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford, Connecticut, the pop star will perform more than 50 dates across the United States before wrapping up the U.S. leg with a 10-concert residency at Barclays Center in Brooklyn in February 2027. Then she's off to Europe. Along the way, she'll be joined by a rotating lineup of opening acts including Wolf Alice, Devon Again, and The Last Dinner Party. And mark your calendars: her third studio album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, drops on June 12. Tickets went on sale through Live Nation and Ticketmaster, but many dates are already sold out or close to it. That's where third-party resale sites come in. StubHub, SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, TicketNetwork, Gametime, and Event Tickets Center all have tickets available. Prices vary, but as of now, the lowest we've seen is $141 on Vivid Seats. These sites guarantee authentic tickets delivered digitally to your phone or email. So if you're hoping to see Olivia live, don't wait—these seats won't last long.
why_it_matters: This story shows how difficult it has become for young fans to buy concert tickets at normal prices, as resale markets often inflate costs, raising questions about fairness and access to live music.

background_read: Olivia Rodrigo burst onto the music scene in 2021 with her debut single "drivers license," which shattered streaming records and earned her several Grammy Awards. Her previous SOUR Tour quickly sold out, mirroring the intense demand for live pop music today.

Ticketmaster and Live Nation are the dominant companies selling primary tickets for major concerts in the U.S., but their systems often crash or sell out in minutes, pushing fans toward secondary markets.
Resale platforms like StubHub and SeatGeek provide a marketplace where ticket holders can resell tickets, but prices can surge far above the original face value due to high demand.
Barclays Center, where the residency will take place, is a multi-purpose arena in Brooklyn that opened in 2012 and is home to the NBA's Brooklyn Nets.

perspectives.description: Resale sites give fans a second chance to get tickets after the official sale sells out, and digital verification ensures the tickets are not fraudulent.
Prices on third-party sites are often much higher than face value, which can lock out fans with less money and reward scalpers who bulk-buy tickets.
The secondary ticket market is a natural result of limited supply and huge demand for star artists; it's a complex economic system that tech platforms have scaled globally.
Some governments and event organizers are exploring laws against ticket bots and price caps to make live events more accessible for regular fans.
